headline: Panama is the latest country hit by a major quake

sources.title: Two powerful earthquakes, multiple aftershocks, rock Panama (AP News)
M 7.7 - 12 km WSW of Pitaloza Arriba, Panama (USGS)
Earthquake causes destruction and deaths in western Colombia (AP News)
Colombia and Venezuela quakes are unconnected despite similar magnitude, experts say (MercoPress)
Panama hit with 7.7 magnitude earthquake (video, CBS News)

chunks.text: On October 9, 2026, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck a [[remote]] area of central Panama just before 1 p.m. [[local time]]. The U.S. Geological Survey first measured it at magnitude 8, then [[revised]] the number. The quake was [[shallow]], and people felt it as far away as Colombia. A magnitude 6.6 quake followed that afternoon. Office workers in Panama City {{cleared out}} of their buildings [[as a precaution]]. The shaking also {{set off}} [[tsunami warnings]], which were later lifted.

verbs.why: The students cleared out of the room when the alarm rang. People cleared out of the park when the storm started. Office workers in Panama City cleared out of their buildings as a precaution.

verbs.wrong: To count the size of a wave
verbs.why: Smoke from the toast set off the fire alarm. One small mistake set off a long argument. The shaking set off tsunami warnings for several countries.

chunks.text: Officials said most of the damage was in three central provinces. They reported no damage in the [[capital]]. The quake {{knocked down}} part of a cathedral's [[bell tower]] in one city. Deep [[cracks]] {{showed up}} on some roads. Several people were hurt, but no deaths were reported at first. The main airport {{shut down}} for a while and reopened that afternoon. Panama Canal teams {{looked over}} their [[facilities]] for damage, and work there {{carried on}} normally.

verbs.correct: To make something fall to the ground
verbs.wrong: To ring a church bell loudly
verbs.why: The strong wind knocked down a tree on our street. The storm knocked down power lines across the town. The quake knocked down part of a cathedral's bell tower in central Panama.

verbs.correct: To appear or become easy to see
verbs.wrong: To be fixed by road workers
verbs.why: A small crack showed up in the kitchen wall. Spots showed up on the leaves after the rain. Deep cracks showed up on some roads after the quake.

verbs.correct: To stop working for a time
verbs.why: The school shut down for two days because of snow. The subway shut down during the storm. Panama's main airport shut down for a while after the quake.
Can you look over my essay before I send it? The mechanic looked over the car's brakes. Teams at the Panama Canal looked over its facilities for damage.
After the short rain, the game carried on. The teacher carried on with the lesson when the noise stopped. Work at the Panama Canal carried on normally after the quake.

chunks.text: Panama is the third country in the region to {{go through}} a major earthquake since June. On June 24, quakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck northern Venezuela one after the other. The Associated Press reports that they killed more than 6,500 people. On August 10, a magnitude 7.4 quake killed at least 289 people in western Colombia. In Cali, [[search teams]] {{picked through}} the [[rubble]] of fallen buildings.

verbs.why: She went through a lot when her father was sick. Many families went through hard times last winter. Panama is the third country in the region to go through a major earthquake since June.

verbs.wrong: To mark a building as unsafe
verbs.why: She picked through the box of old photos. He picked through the pile of papers to find his ticket. In Cali, search teams picked through the rubble of fallen buildings.

chunks.text: Scientists say several [[tectonic plates]] {{come together}} near Panama, so earthquakes are common there. [[Pressure]] {{builds up}} where plates meet and is [[released]] in quakes. Still, the Venezuela and Colombia quakes {{turned out}} to have different causes. A scientist at Colombia's national earthquake network explained the difference. The Venezuelan quakes were shallow, with plates moving [[sideways]]. The Colombian quake was much deeper, where one plate sinks beneath another. Experts say the two events were not connected.

verbs.why: The two rivers come together just north of the city. The two main roads come together at a small square. Several tectonic plates come together near Panama.
Snow built up on the roof all week. Dust builds up quickly under the bed. Pressure builds up where the plates meet.
The strange noise turned out to be a cat. The test turned out to be easy. The quakes in Venezuela and Colombia turned out to have different causes.

mainIdea.s: A strong earthquake hit central Panama, damaging old buildings and forcing people outside. Scientists say many plates meet in this region, but the earlier quakes nearby were not linked.
mainIdea.why: A magnitude 7.7 quake struck central Panama, and workers cleared out of buildings. Experts say the Venezuela and Colombia quakes turned out to have different causes.

mainIdea.s: Panama was shaken by a major quake that damaged churches and roads in several provinces. Experts believe it was caused by the June quakes in Venezuela, which put stress on faults close by.
mainIdea.why: Close, but scientists did not link the quakes. A scientist in Colombia said the Venezuela and Colombia quakes turned out to have different causes.

mainIdea.s: Panama has opened a new early warning system that sends alerts to cell phones before shaking starts. Officials say it was tested in several cities with help from local scientists.
mainIdea.why: This is about a magnitude 7.7 quake in central Panama. It follows big quakes in Venezuela in June and in Colombia in August.

tf.s: The shaking set off tsunami warnings for several countries.
tf.why: Tsunami warnings were issued for several countries after the quake, and they were later lifted.

tf.s: The quake knocked down several tall buildings in Panama City.
tf.why: Most of the damage was in three central provinces. The quake knocked down part of a cathedral's bell tower in a central city.

tf.s: Teams at the Panama Canal looked over its facilities for damage.
tf.why: Canal teams checked their facilities for damage, and work there carried on normally.

tf.s: The main airport shut down for a full week after the quake.
tf.why: The airport shut down for a short time and reopened that same afternoon.

tf.s: Search teams in Cali picked through the rubble of fallen buildings.
tf.why: This happened after the magnitude 7.4 quake hit western Colombia on August 10.

tf.s: Scientists say the Venezuela quakes set off the Colombia quake.
tf.why: The two events turned out to have different causes. A scientist in Colombia said the Venezuelan quakes were shallow and the Colombian one was deeper.

lines.text: Did you hear about the earthquake in Panama?
I did. It was a magnitude 7.7, right?
Yes. The first reading was 8, but scientists revised it.
Was it bad in the capital?
Not really. Office workers {{cleared out}} of their buildings, but officials reported no damage there.
[[That's good to hear]]. What about the rest of the country?
The quake {{knocked down}} part of a cathedral's bell tower, and deep cracks {{showed up}} on some roads.
The main airport {{shut down}} for a while, but it reopened that afternoon.
Several people were hurt, but no deaths were reported at first. [[It could have been worse]].
Didn't Venezuela and Colombia have big quakes too?
Yes. Panama is the third country in the region to {{go through}} one since June.
Three big quakes in a few months? [[What are the odds]]?
Scientists say they're not connected. The Venezuela and Colombia quakes {{turned out}} to have different causes.
So why does that region get so many earthquakes?
Several tectonic plates {{come together}} there, and pressure {{builds up}} where they meet.
I hope everyone there can [[stay safe]] during the aftershocks.
